bridgeRouteRisk.summary: cNGN is canonically issued on Bantu and distributed to destination networks through the issuer's bridge architecture. The Bantu Foundation describes Bantu as the single source of truth and states that bridge contracts lock Bantu cNGN and mint equivalent destination representations; cNGN's official API exposes swaps between supported networks. The Ethereum, Base, BSC, Polygon, and Celo deployments are therefore bridge representations, not independent native liabilities. Solana is conservatively classified as a bridge representation because independent native issuance and per-chain reconciliation are unproven, while its exact AMTP relationship remains an evidence gap. Destination owner Safes, the Base proxy upgrade owner, and Solana mint/program authorities remain scoreable under Bridge Risk; AMTP validator, peer, rate-limit, and adapter addresses were not disclosed in the reviewed primary sources.

sources.label: cNGN FAQ — Bantu native issuance and supported networks

routes.reviewNote: The cNGN FAQ says cNGN is natively issued on Bantu, and the Bantu Foundation states that Bantu is the source of truth while bridge contracts lock Bantu cNGN and mint equivalent destination representations. This Ethereum deployment is therefore a Bantu AMTP bridge representation, not an independent Ethereum liability chain. At Ethereum block 25,770,803 on 2026-08-16, symbol() returned cNGN and owner() returned 0x57da45ee907f9d58d781c6ed5abf730eb6673d80; the fixed Safe read recorded a 2/2 owner with the consortium signer pair. No Ethereum-local deposit, collateral, or per-chain reserve reconciliation was evidenced.

The cNGN FAQ and Bantu Foundation case study establish Bantu as the native ledger and describe destination bridge contracts that lock Bantu cNGN and mint equivalent representations. This Base deployment is consequently a bridge representation, not independent Base issuance. At Base block 50,066,095 on 2026-08-16, symbol() returned cNGN and owner() returned 0xc3ebca72b6e3c06833ba81c824de685eb2eff21e; the fixed Safe read recorded the same 2/2 consortium signer pair. The token is an EIP-1967 proxy with implementation 0x941360b66ccb94012e85225639476b43999c6cf3; ProxyAdmin 0x639e6756f129b3bb67961488e10dad3a3380af83 is owned by EOA 0xdd3446ce5aa397fd957460ba03e4538caeeff22e. No Base-local collateral or reserve reconciliation was evidenced.

The Bantu Foundation identifies cNGN as natively minted on Bantu and bridged to other chains through lock-and-mint contracts. This BSC deployment is therefore a Bantu AMTP bridge representation, not independent BSC issuance. At BSC block 116,357,377 on 2026-08-16, symbol() returned cNGN and owner() returned 0x555ad4b8aacdb16afd2ed4d334f51614222a9f0b; the fixed Safe read recorded a 2/2 Safe with the same consortium signer pair. No BSC-local deposit, collateral, or per-chain reserve reconciliation was evidenced.

The cNGN FAQ and Bantu Foundation case study establish Bantu as the native source of truth and destination chains as bridge distributions. This Polygon deployment is therefore a Bantu AMTP bridge representation. At Polygon block 92,151,009 on 2026-08-16, symbol() returned cNGN and owner() returned 0xce6720dd9076aa67053abb27ecbd613a5867d1ba; the fixed Safe read recorded a 2/2 Safe with the consortium signer pair. No Polygon-local deposit, collateral, or per-chain reserve reconciliation was evidenced.

The cNGN FAQ and Bantu Foundation case study establish Bantu as the native source of truth and destination chains as bridge distributions. This Celo deployment is therefore a Bantu AMTP bridge representation, not independent Celo issuance. At Celo block 75,053,963 on 2026-08-17, the live cNGN contract had owner Safe 0xe8c11f6168aa035620f7f14efba0c86d3b11c047 with threshold 2 and the same consortium signer pair as the other reviewed EVM destinations. No Celo-local deposit, collateral, or per-chain reserve reconciliation was evidenced.

routes.protocol: cNGN Solana issuance program / Bantu route under review
routes.reviewNote: Conservative representation classification: the Solana Token-2022 mint is not treated as native issuance because the reviewed primary sources do not prove an independent Solana liability ledger, local collateral, or per-chain reserve reconciliation. The cNGN FAQ and official bridge API identify Bantu and supported-network swaps, while the Bantu Foundation documents the issuer's lock-and-mint architecture; however, the Solana-specific AMTP adapter, peers, and burn/lock reconciliation remain undisclosed. The route therefore remains scoreable as a representation while its exact bridge implementation is an evidence gap.
